content:
One note upfront: this Read stands on 21 days of data last updated 2026-03-28 — 76 days ago — so treat everything here as a March snapshot, not a live picture.

In March, £1,150 of your £1,554 tracked spend was a single rent payment — 74% of everything recorded, in one transaction on 9 March. Strip that out and the remaining £404 breaks down to **shopping** at £185, **groceries** at £131, **utilities & bills** at £54, and **eating & drinking out** at £22. That's the full picture of where your money went.

With only 8 transactions across 21 days, the data is too thin to call anything a pattern. What's clear is that your free cash flow sits at £1,950 against £1,150 in fixed costs — but with one month on file, it's impossible to say how consistently the remaining £404 in variable spend holds, or whether March was light, heavy, or typical.

The most useful next move is anchoring what you actually want this money to do. No goal is set yet, which means there's nothing to measure the £1,950 against.

[CTA:supply_input]Set my first savings goal[/CTA]

— C.
